the transcription of both pro-apoptotic and anti-apoptosis genes is increased in patients with septic shock compared with healthy controls.
the apoptosis profiles of circulating leukocytes are altered in a cell-specific pattern during sepsis.
in patients with severe sepsis and septic shock, apoptosis is increased in granulocytes and monocytes, while CD+4 T lymphocytes show increased expression of pro-apoptotic genes.

the expression of pro- and anti- apoptosis related genes in patients with septic shock.
the molecular mechanisms underlying apoptosis and the role of apoptosis regulators in the pathogenesis of sepsis and septic shock.
the identification of gene expression profiles that may be used to monitor the progression of sepsis.

the apoptosis of leukocytes in sepsis is not a simple phenomenon, but rather a complex and multifaceted one, in which different cell populations are involved.
the apoptosis of immune cells in sepsis is not a simple on/off switch, but rather a complex, cell-specific process.
apoptosis in patients with septic shock is a complex and cell-specific process, which is not restricted to one cell type or one pathway.

sepsis is associated with an increased expression of pro- and antiapoptotic genes in circulating leukocytes, which is cell-specific.
in sepsis, there is a dysregulation in apoptosis of peripheral blood leukocytes, which occurs in a cell-specific fashion.
